title: OTT Releases Streaming on This Weekend April 18th 2025 Full List
summary: This weekend brings a packed OTT lineup across languages and platforms: horror, thrillers, rom-coms, prestige TV, documentaries and regional drama. Major releases include The Last of Us Season 2, Netflix Originals, Hindi and regional Indian titles on Prime, ZEE5 and Hotstar, plus international noir and true-crime. Plenty of choices for every mood.
content:
April is on fire! From ancient kingdoms to haunted forests, quirky salons to AI nightmares — this weekend’s OTT slate is hot. Need a watchlist boost? You’re in the right place.

Khauf (Hindi | April 18 | Amazon Prime Video)Enter a haunted Delhi hostel where fear is lurking in every corner. Monika Panwar and Rajat Kapoor lead the charge in this psychological horror-social commentary. Disturbing, claustrophobic and unforgettable.

Logout (Hindi | April 18 | ZEE5)Babil Khan plays an influencer whose phone is stolen by an obsessed fan — and that’s just the beginning. A chilling take on toxic fame, Logout is a tech-age thriller with paranoia and punch.

Mere Husband Ki Biwi (Hindi | April 18 | Jio Hotstar)Arjun Kapoor, Bhumi Pednekar and Rakul Preet Singh bring love, laughs and retrograde amnesia into a crazy rom-com. Who loves who? Who remembers what? Find out in this madcap relationship rollercoaster.

The Last of Us – Season 2 (English | April 14 | Jio Hotstar)The apocalypse continues. Ellie, Joel and a new character Abby clash in a season that’s more brutal, more emotional and even more cinematic. High stakes, heartbreak and infected horrors await.

Ransom Canyon (English | April 17 | Netflix)A ranches, rivalries and romance saga. Josh Duhamel and Minka Kelly star in this Western epic set in small town Texas where love and legacy collide.

The Glass Dome (Swedish | April 15 | Netflix)A policewoman with a dark past. A city wrapped in lies. This Scandinavian noir has twists, trauma and tension in every frame. Sharp, stylish and very addictive.

Oklahoma City Bombing: American Terror (English | April 18 | Netflix)This docuseries revisits the 1995 tragedy with chilling clarity. Personal testimonies, archived footage and haunting revelations. A must watch for true crime and history buffs.

Daveed (Tamil | April 18 | ZEE5)A tough guy with a good heart, stuck between the underworld and redemption. This Tamil action drama packs emotional punches along with street fights.

Istanbul Encyclopedia (Turkish | April 17 | Netflix)A multi-generational, multi-class saga in Turkey. Family feuds, secrets and cityscapes. Think drama with depth.

Ghaati (Marathi | April 18 | Amazon Prime Video)Rural Maharashtra, caste conflict and a murder mystery. This socio-political drama is raw, rooted and relevant.

Government Cheese (English | April 16 | Apple TV+)David Oyelowo is haunted by visions. This trippy dramedy is about race, trauma and spirituality.

Shotyi Bole Shotyi Kichhu Nei (Bengali | April 18 | Hoichoi)A family torn apart by lies, secrets and guilt. This emotional drama unfolds layer by layer with heartbreak and honesty.

Murmur (Tamil | April 17 | Lionsgate Play)A small town crime story with a creepy atmosphere. Whispers, betrayals and moral dilemmas. Quiet cinema done right.

So many titles. So little time.

Whether you’re in the mood for mythology, a psychological ride or just some romantic chaos — this weekend’s OTT has you covered. Clear your schedule, cancel those plans and dive into stories that thrill, move and maybe mess with your mind a little.
